articles_used.title: Toyota, Nissan, and Honda to Standardize Parts to Lower Costs
articles_used.full_text:
Japan’s automakers will work together to lower production costs as they band together to compete against China’s growing automotive sector.
Japan’s three largest automakers have agreed to begin standardizing vehicle parts in an effort to reduce costs, according toAutomotive News. The outlet reports that Japan Automobile Manufacturers Association chairman Koji Sato, who is also the vice chairman of Toyota, announced the decision at a news conference in Tokyo this week.
In the short term, the standardization efforts will begin with unified quality criteria for steel, consistent protocols for plastics and resins, and a universal color-coding scheme for wiring harnesses. In the long term, the Japan Automobile Manufacturers Association has plans to move to more components that cover the entire car. The three areas were chosen as the first to be standardized because they are parts that are generally not noticed by consumers, and they shouldn’t have an impact on any brand’s individual identity. All three are also areas that account for significant production costs for the automakers, meaning they can have an immediate impact.
See all results forused Toyota for salenear 59100
The first discussions of standardization are set to include Japan’s domestic automotive parts suppliers, though international suppliers will be brought into the fold in time. The first standardization efforts are set to go into place next year, according to theANreport.
The push to simplify and lower costs comes as Japan’s seven automakers, including Toyota, Nissan, Honda, Mazda, Subaru, Mitsubishi, and Suzuki, work to fend off the increasingly competitive list of Chinese automakers. The automakers are said to hope that they can channel the money saved by homogenizing into new innovations.
“We all share this strong sense of crisis, creating a momentum for change,” Sato said. “Based upon our sense of a crisis, we decided to choose these three areas.”

By hounding his college professors at the University of Wisconsin-Milwaukee, he was able to travel Wisconsin seeking out stories in the auto world before landing his dream job atCar and Driver. His new goal is to delay the inevitable demise of his 2010 Volkswagen Golf.

articles_used.title: IG Metall weitet Warnstreiks in norddeutscher Metall- und Elektroindustrie aus
articles_used.summary_raw: Bundesweit hatten am Freitag Beschäftigte der Metall- und Elektroindustrie ihre Arbeit niedergelegt. Im Norden will die IG Metall Küste jetzt nachlegen: Nochmal soll für 24 Stunden gestreikt werden - teils schon ab heute Abend.
articles_used.full_text:
Inhalte zeigen von:
Externe Anbieter:
Stand: 22.11.2026 • 04:50 Uhr
Bundesweit hatten am Freitag Beschäftigte der Metall- und Elektroindustrie ihre Arbeit niedergelegt. Im Norden will die IG Metall Küste jetzt nachlegen: Nochmal soll für 24 Stunden gestreikt werden - teils schon ab heute Abend.
NachWarnstreiks am Freitaghat die IG Metall Küste weitere 24-stündige Arbeitsniederlegungen in Norddeutschland angekündigt, die teilweise am Sonntagabend und in der Nacht beginnen sollen. Das teilte der Bezirk Küste mit, der für Nordniedersachsen, Bremen, Hamburg, Schleswig-Holstein und Mecklenburg-Vorpommern zuständig ist.
Nach Gewerkschaftsangaben treffe das unter anderem die Mercedes-Werke in Bremen und Hamburg, die Meyer Werft in Papenburg sowie den Windkraftanlagenhersteller Siemens Gamesa in Cuxhaven. Insgesamt sind mehr als 23.000 Beschäftigte in 19 Betrieben aufgerufen, die Arbeit niederzulegen.
FAQ20.11.2026
Für die Volkswagen-Beschäftigten beginnt kommende Woche eine harte Tarifrunde.mehr
Die Tarifverhandlungen für rund 130.000 Beschäftigte der norddeutschen Metall- und Elektroindustrie hatten am 8. Oktober begonnen. Bislang ist es in Norddeutschland wie auch in den anderen Tarifgebieten nach drei Verhandlungsrunden nicht zu einer Einigung gekommen. Eine vierte Verhandlungsrunde vereinbarten die Tarifparteien im Norden noch nicht "Wir legen jetzt noch einmal deutlich nach", sagte Daniel Friedrich, Bezirksleiter und Verhandlungsführer der IG Metall Küste. "Die Arbeitgeber müssen sich bewegen."
Die IG Metall fordert bei einer einjährigen Laufzeit fünf Prozent mehr Geld für die Beschäftigten. Gesamtmetall bietet eine Einmalzahlung, die aber unter bestimmten Bedingungen ausgesetzt werden kann, sowie 1,3 Prozent mehr Geld zum Juli 2028. Die Laufzeit soll nach Vorstellung der Arbeitgeber 26 Monate betragen.

articles_used.title: Mexican drug lord on FBI's 10 most wanted list arrested in shoot-out
articles_used.summary_raw: Fausto Isidro "Chapo Idisro" Meza Flores, who is accused of drug trafficking and torture, is detained after gun fight with authorities.
articles_used.full_text:
This video can not be played
Watch: Suspected drug lord 'El Chapo Isidro' transferred to Mexico's capital
A Mexican drug lord who was on the FBI's 10 most wanted list has been arrested following a shoot-out with Mexican authorities.
Fausto Isidro "Chapo Isidro" Meza Flores and seven others were detained by Mexican special forces in Guasave, Sinaloa on Friday, Mexico's defence secretariat said.
Seven suspects were killed in the operation, as were four members of the Mexican army who were travelling to reinforce security in Guasave, the secretariat added.
Meza Flores was wanted in Mexico on organised crime charges, while he has been accused of "flooding the US with fentanyl, cocaine, heroin and other deadly drugs" by the FBI. The US is seeking his extradition.
Mexico has stepped up efforts to tackle drug-related crime after coming under pressure from US President Donald Trump since he returned to the White House.
Meza Flores, the leader of the Meza Flores Organisation, also known as the Guasave Cartel, is thought to have been active in the drug trafficking trade since the 1990s but managed to evade authorities till now by maintaining a relatively low profile.
Fausto Isidro "Chapo Isidro" Meza Flores was detained by Mexican special forces on Friday
Using US intelligence on his whereabouts, Mexican special forces descended on his location using "stealth and surprise", establishing a perimeter to prevent him from escaping and reinforcements arriving, Mexico's defence secretariat said.
However, they "came under attack from gunfire and explosives" before entering the property and arresting Meza Flores, the secretariat continued.
Videos circulating online appear to show helicopters firing streams of bullets towards the ground in Guasave. Others appear to show people at a baseball stadium fleeing as they hear shooting sounds.
Eight people in total were arrested, including Meza Flores' second-in-command, who is also his cousin, and his brother-in-law, who is the group's financial operator, the secretariat added.
This video can not be played
Watch: Moment Mexican reporter takes cover on air as gunshots ring out nearby
Meza Flores, his cousin, and his brother-in-law were flown to Mexico City to face prosecution, the defence secretariat said. The other five remained in the state of Sinaloa.
Authorities also said they had seized multiple weapons during the operation, including a grenade launcher, as well as drugs and cash.
The US Consulate General in the city of Hermosillo said it was "monitoring reports of ongoing security operations, armed clashes, road blockades, and vehicle fires that occurred overnight in Ahome, Guamúchil, Guasave, and Navolato" following the arrest of Meza-Flores.
It advised US citizens to remain alert for potential violence in the area and for residents to remain sheltered in place.
When Meza Flores was added to the FBI's most-wanted list in 2025, he was accused of "heinous crimes" including kidnapping, extortion and torture.
Then-acting FBI director Brian Driscoll said Meza Flores and his organisation had also unleashed a "scourge of illicit drugs" into the US via its southern border with Mexico.
He was initially charged with drug trafficking in the US in 2012 before being charged again in 2019.
The 44-year-old is alleged to have conspired to manufacture and distribute large quantities of cocaine, heroin, methamphetamine and marijuana between 2005 and 2019.
A number of vehicles were pictured burning on a highway near Los Mochis, Sinaloa, after Fausto Isidro "Chapo Idisro" Meza Flores was arrested
Meza Flores was originally a high-ranking member of the Beltrán Leyva Organization, but a split between rival factions led to a surge of violence and prompted him to establish his own cartel by 2013.
His organisation has also engaged in what US officials described as an "extremely violent turf war" with the Sinaloa Cartel, one of the most powerful drug trafficking gangs, which operates in the same region.
Meza Flores was added to the FBI's most-wanted list after Mexican authorities reportedly linked his cartel to 20 million fentanyl pills they seized in 2024.
Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum has taken a tougher stance on the country's cartels in a bid to resist US intervention on Mexican soil. Mexico has welcomed closer collaboration but resisted US boots on the ground.
Trump made stemming the flow of drugs into the US across its southern border one of his key election pledges.

We are notifying customers about a security incident involving a subset of prompts submitted to Together AI’s serverless inference service in June and July 2026. An unauthorized party downloaded stored prompt samples after a credential for a private repository was exposed in a public code repository.
We apologize for this incident. We are reviewing the affected data to determine what information was exposed and which customers require direct notification.
As part of routine software testing, we collected prompt samples authorized for that use and stored them in a private Hugging Face repository. The samples came from requests to the MiniMax M3, GLM-5.2, and Kimi K2.6 models, primarily on June 24, July 4, July 8, and July 14, 2026.
During development of our public GitHub repository, xorl, an AI coding agent committed a credential that provided access to the private Hugging Face repository. Our automated scanning detected the exposed credential, and we reverted the commit.
During the exposure window, an unauthorized party obtained the credential and used it to download the stored prompt samples. The party subsequently searched those samples for credentials to other services and tested whether those credentials were valid. Five of the credentials tested were canary credentials associated with a Dragos security experiment.
We have no reason to believe the unauthorized party has leaked this data further and understand that it has now been deleted.
We have worked with an external forensic investigation firm and law enforcement to investigate the incident.
Based on our review, we have not identified evidence of additional prompt leakage beyond this incident. Our review of the affected prompt contents is ongoing to determine whether sensitive personal information or other customer data was exposed. We will contact affected customers directly as needed with the findings relevant to them.

Customers handling sensitive prompt data should enable ZDR in their account settings.

articles_used.title: Klimakonferenz in Antalya: Neuer Entwurf soll den Durchbruch bringen
articles_used.summary_raw: Eigentlich sollte die COP31 Freitag enden - doch die fast 200 Staaten ringen in der Türkei weiter um eine Abschlusserklärung. Streitpunkt ist der Ausstieg aus fossilen Energien. Ein neuer Entwurf stimmt das Gastgeberland optimistisch.
articles_used.full_text:
Inhalte zeigen von:
Externe Anbieter:
Stand: 22.11.2026 • 02:55 Uhr
Eigentlich sollte die COP31 Freitag enden - doch die fast 200 Staaten ringen in der Türkei weiter um eine Abschlusserklärung. Streitpunkt ist der Ausstieg aus fossilen Energien. Ein neuer Entwurf stimmt das Gastgeberland optimistisch.
Bis tief in die Nacht rangen Verhandlungsgruppen im türkischen Antalya mit der Präsidentschaft der UN-Klimakonferenz um Formulierungen für eine Abschlusserklärung. Gegen ein Uhr Ortszeit kündigte der COP31-Präsident Murat Kurum einen neuen Textentwurf an. "Wir glauben, dass wir einen Text vorgelegt haben, dem alle Vertragsstaaten zustimmen können", sagte er.
Die Delegationen sollen ihn nun prüfen. Am Vormittag wollen die Vertreter von mehr als 190 Staaten darüber beraten und abstimmen.
Kurum rief die Delegierten auf, Kompromisse zu schließen und den Klimaschutz schneller voranzubringen. Er verwies zudem auf Fortschritte bei Verhandlungen über den Ausbau sauberer Energien und über Finanzhilfen für Länder, die besonders stark unter den Folgen des Klimawandels leiden. Ob es in Antalya zu einem Beschluss kommt, ist weiter offen.
21.11.2026
Dass eine UN-Klimakonferenz pünktlich endet, passiert praktisch nie. Doch droht die COP31 zu scheitern?mehr
Die Konferenz hätte planmäßig am Freitag enden sollen. Die Unterhändler verhandelten den ganzen Samstag hindurch bis in die frühen Morgenstunden des Sonntags.
Eine Einigung scheiterte bislang vor allem am Streit über fossile Energien. Die EU, kleine Inselstaaten und zahlreiche weitere Länder wollen die Abkehr von Kohle, Öl und Gas ausdrücklich in der Abschlusserklärung festschreiben. Ein zuvor vorgelegter Entwurf enthielt dieses Bekenntnis jedoch nicht mehr. Ölexportierende Staaten wie Saudi-Arabien lehnen eine solche Formulierung ab. Kritiker warnen deshalb vor einem Rückschritt gegenüber dem Beschluss der Weltklimakonferenz in Dubai 2023.
COP31-Präsident Kurum ging nun davon aus, dass die Bedenken in diesem Punkt ausgeräumt seien. Das gelte auch für die Frage, wie Entwicklungsländer bei derAnpassung an den Klimawandel finanziell unterstütztwerden, sagte er.
20.11.2026
Bei der Weltklimakonferenz in Antalya beziehen auch Bundestagsabgeordnete Stellung.mehr
Die diesjährige Konferenz ist die erste,seit das UN-Umweltprogramm bestätigt hat, dass die Erderwärmung die Schwelle von 1,5 Grad Celsius höchstwahrscheinlich überschreiten wird. Alle Staaten hatten sich vor mehr als zehn Jahren darauf verständigt, den Temperaturanstieg möglichst auf diesen Wert zu begrenzen. Bei einer stärkeren Erwärmung verschärfen sich die Folgen extremer Wetterereignisse.
Mit Informationen von Dietrich Karl Mäurer, ARD Hauptstadtstudio, zur Zeit in Antalya

articles_used.title: FBI reportedly investigating apparent hack of its criminal database
articles_used.summary_raw: The National Crime Information Center database is used by federal and local law enforcement to share information.
articles_used.full_text:
The FBI is investigating an apparent breach of its criminal information database, US media reports, citing two people briefed on the issue.
The National Crime Information Center (NCIC) database is used by federal and local law enforcement to share information on warrants and background checks.
It would not be the first time hackers have targeted the FBI, the domestic intelligence and security service of the US. The agency did not respond to the BBC's request for comment.
When asked about the breach in a Fox News interview on Saturday, President Donald Trump said he had "just heard" about the hack. "I will say that it's not good. I don't like that," he said.
"But maybe we'll learn things that we would've never learned otherwise," Trump added.
This apparent breach of FBI database comes after a string of tech outages which hit banking, air traffic control and other sectors in the US last week. Officials have said they were not caused by cyber-attacks, but the blackouts have sparked scrutiny from lawmakers.
White House National Cyber Director Sean Cairncross was fired this week,with Trump saying he was not good enough.
Dan Lorhmann, a former analyst for the National Security Agency (NSA), told the BBC News Channel that the NCIC's data included "critical information relating to nationwide criminal activity" and needed to be protected.
He added that while US security agencies including the FBI have "an amazing ability" to keep such information safe" and are "globally respected", the level of cyber-attacks is rising globally.
"There's a lot of different reasons why that's happening but I do have faith in our experts in government," Lorhmann said.
In September,the FBI said it was investigating an apparent breachby a cyber-crime group ShinyHunters, which claimed it had stolen sensitive information on all bureau staff - around 38,000 people.
After that hack, one former FBI agent told the BBC he feared for the safety of current employees, whose personal information could soon become available online to criminals and hostile nation-state hackers.
In a separate development, NBC reported an apparent cyberattack against the US Department of Agriculture (USDA).
Employees were informed on Thursday that its farm payment system had been targeted, NBC said.
The USDA has not publicly commented on the issue.

articles_used.title: Since last year, we asked: "What if AI solved the Riemann Hypothesis?"
Nigerian youth have shown their power in the past - why aren't they shaping this election?
articles_used.summary_raw: Fewer young people have registered to vote in next year's election than in 2023 - are young people losing faith in democracy?
articles_used.full_text:
Bola Tinubu (in red hat) would be 79 at the end of a second term, if he is re-elected
Abdulhadi Dalhatu is something of a rarity in Nigeria politics.
At 38, he is among the young people seeking elected office in a country where about 80% of the population is under 40.
He hopes his age will stand in his favour as he campaigns for a seat in the state assembly in the northern Kano state in January's general elections.
"Younger people are the majority in this country and should be deciding the future," Dalhatu tells the BBC.
But Nigeria's political history suggests he faces an uphill battle.
Since the return to civilian rule in 1999, Goodluck Jonathan has been the youngest person elected president, taking office at the age of 53.
The current president, Bola Tinubu, is 74 and would be 79 by the end of a second term if he is re-elected in January.
His main challengers are also considerably older. Atiku Abubakar, seeking the presidency for the seventh time, is 79, while Peter Obi is 65.
Of the 18 presidential candidates, only one is under 40 - Moses Olusoji Adebisi, a 35-year-old businessman representing the Democratic Leadership Alliance (DLA).
Although he says he is confident of winning, few Nigerians appear to know much about him and he has not been seen much on the campaign trail.
The contrast is striking in a country with one of the world's youngest populations, where young people have repeatedly demonstrated their ability to shape political debate and mobilise for change.
In the previous election, Obi, then 61, galvanised millions of young Nigerians through a social media-driven movement known as the "Obedients".
His campaign promised a break from the established political order, appealing particularly to young people struggling to find jobs and earn a decent living.
But his failure to win the presidency left many of his supporters disillusioned.
"At the time we were so hopeful, but unfortunately the result wasn't what we wanted, which made many lose hope in the system," former Obedient Nonso Chukwudi tells the BBC.
The movement had built on the momentum of the EndSars protests in 2020, which grew into one of Nigeria's biggest youth-led movement in decades.
Initially sparked by anger over police brutality, the demonstrators developed into a wider call for political reform, accountability and greater youth participation in governance.
But the protests were eventually crushed by the authorities. About 56 were reportedly killed, although officials dispute this figure, while hundreds were arrested and some had their bank accounts frozen.
Both EndSars and the Obedients demonstrated the capacity of young Nigerians to mobile around political causes.
Abdulhadi Dalhatu hopes to be president one day but bemoans the financial obstacles needed to contest
But turning that enthusiasm into sustained electoral participation has proved much harder.
Hajara Musa, 33, is among those who have lost faith in the political system. She has no plans to register or vote in the near future.
"I just feel like things are already determined and I'll just be wasting my time. It is going to be the same people all over again," she tells the BBC.
The electoral register appears to reflect this growing disillusionment.
Although the number of registered voters has increased by 10 million to over 103 million since the last election, enrolment of those under 35 has actually fallen, by about seven million.
Young people now account for just 29% of registered voters, down from 40% in 2023.
Nigeria's electoral commission, Inec, says it has made efforts to encourage more young people to register ahead of the 2027 general elections.
This includes appointing nine ambassadors from the entertainment industry, spanning film, music and comedy, to reach younger audiences.
But the figures suggest these efforts have yet to make a significant difference.
Dalhatu says he understands the frustration but argues that young Nigerians cannot expect change, if they stay away from the political process.
"Unfortunately, many prefer to just post on social media" instead of getting involved, he says.
Of course being young does not mean you are necessarily the best candidate.
For those who want to participate, there is a formidable obstacle to getting into politics - money.
Young people now account for just 29% of registered voters, down from 40% in 2023
Dalhatu dreams of becoming president one day, but says he has previously had to abandon campaigns because he could not raise enough funds.
The cost of running for office in Nigeria is notoriously high.
Under the Electoral Act, presidential candidates were allowed to spend up to 5bn naira (£2.8m; $3.7m) on campaigns ahead of the 2023 elections. That spending limit has since been doubled.
The cost of nomination forms alone puts the presidency beyond the reach of most aspiring young Nigerians.
The ruling All Progressive Congress (APC), along with the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) and the African Democratic Congress (ADC) have each set their presidential nomination fee at 100m naira ($74,000; £56,000), making it extremely hard for new challengers to emerge.
Since the return to democracy in 1999, only two parties have governed Nigeria - the PDP from 1999 to 2015 and the APC since 2015.
These parties, alongside the ADC, formed last year by politicians who had defected from the other two, have established nationwide network of branches, supporters and campaigners.
Those aspiring candidates without the financial resources to secure nomination forms and compete in the internal party contests of the main parties have little chances of becoming president.
The barriers are also evident in the National Assembly.
Not one of Nigeria's 109 senators is under 40, while only 14 of the 360 members of the House of Representatives fall into that age group.
"I have been in politics for many years and I will tell you that young people in this country lack the resources to become president," says Dalhatu, who is running under Obi's Nigeria Democratic Congress.
Atiku Abubakar is seeking the presidency for a seventh time
Fatima Zahra Umar, a young politician in the APC who has previously tried to run for a seat in the House of Representatives, agrees.
"Young Nigerians are poor. Nigerian politics is cash-intensive, so participation is guided by money," she says, adding that young people are often content with having a bit of influence as a special advisor to a senior politician.
Butpolitical analyst Seun Ajayi believes the problems go beyond the financial barriers.
"We have some of the most brilliant young persons in the world, but they are either not interested in politics or feel satisfied when given a small role in government," he says.
"The old men are not going to sit idle and allow us to push them out. We have to fight for the big positions, but at the moment I don't see the zeal."
Umar believes changing attitudes towards young leadership is equally important.
"Culturally, we are not primed to trust or accept the brilliance of a younger person, so it will be very difficult," she says.
"Old men are still holding on to the system."
Some Nigerians took inspiration from the wave of success of young candidates in the recent midterm elections in the US,some of whom have roots in Africa.
"America Has Done It, Can Nigerians Do the Same?" entertainer Charly Boy wrote on X, in a post that was widely shared.
He said the US results served as a warning to Nigerian politicians that no matter how powerful the political machine, voters can change the direction of government.
He called on young people to interrogate candidates about their past promises: "Has life improved? Where are the jobs, security and affordable living?
"Democracy is not a spectator sport, nor is it about sharing rice," he wrote.

articles_used.title: The Most Popular Car Colors in America
articles_used.full_text:
White was the most popular car color 30 years ago and it maintains that ranking today. When combined with the prominence of black (23.4%) and gray (22.9%), the top three most popular colors hold 72% of market share for modern car colors. It’s worth noting that silver, the fourth grayscale color, has gained just over 1 percentage point in popularity over the past 30 years, moving from 7.3% to 8.4% market share since 1996. Silver now trails blue, which holds 9.1% market share.Most Popular Car Colors by Market Share: 2025 vs. 1996 - iSeeCars StudyRankColor20251996% Change1White25.7%22.1%16.7%2Black23.4%14.2%64.5%3Gray22.9%3.6%528.4%4Blue9.1%10.2%-10.8%5Silver8.4%7.3%14.3%6Red7.0%20.1%-65.2%7Green2.2%13.4%-83.8%8Brown0.4%2.9%-84.6%9Beige0.4%1.6%-73.8%10Orange0.3%0.2%2.5%11Yellow0.1%0.3%-59.4%12Gold0.0%2.3%-98.1%13Purple0.0%0.7%-94.7%Grayscale colors*80.4%47.3%70.1%Non-grayscale colors19.6%51.7%-62.2%*Grayscale colors are black, gray, silver, and white.
iSeeCars analyzed the colors of over 22 million used cars from model years 1996 - 2025 sold from January 2025 to May 2026 to determine the market share for each color.
Gray followed a different path, increasing in market share consistently through the entire period, ultimately rising from only 3.6% to 22.9% and nearly matching black.
Black and white, which were always popular colors, also gained substantial market share, with black’s popularity growing mostly in the early 2000s’ model years and white gaining share starting in the 2010 model year. Conversely, red and green, which ranked as the 2nd and 4th most popular colors in the 1996 model year, declined substantially throughout much of the 30-year period, with each color’s market share now in single digits. Most other colors either lost what little market share they had or maintained their relatively low popularity. Orange was the only non-grayscale color to increase in popularity, though it remains rare at just 0.3% market share.
“The rise of grayscale cars had to come from somewhere, and it was primarily the fall of red and green, though nearly every non-grayscale shade has lost ground since 1996,” said Brauer.
“Trucks are seeing much more than a touch of gray, with the segment going from less than 1 gray truck in 20 in 1996 to 1 in 5 today,” said Brauer.
“SUV market share has grown more than any other vehicle segment since 1996, but SUV color diversity went the opposite direction during that timeframe,” said Brauer.
“Gray has gained ground in every vehicle segment, and it’s the most dominant color for today’s passenger cars,” said Brauer.
“Relative to every other vehicle segment, sports cars still offer a veritable rainbow of color diversity, illustrating the expressive nature of these vehicles and their owners,” said Brauer.
Methodology
iSeeCars analyzed the colors of over 22 million used cars from model years 1996 - 2025 sold from January 2025 to May 2026. The share of each color within each model year was calculated, as was the difference in share between model years 1996 and 2025.

articles_used.title: How a teen gamer and his mother helped rescue a missing girl
articles_used.summary_raw: When 16-year-old Landon Tresp met a teenage girl in an online game, it led to him and his mother helping the FBI rescue her from kidnapping.
articles_used.full_text:
Landon Tresp, 16, left, met the girl playing Among Us before alerting his mother, Khristina, 41, to the missing teen's predicament
Sixteen-year-old Landon Tresp was in the bedroom of his family's Colorado mountain home, playing an online game after finishing his daily chores, when he began chatting on his laptop with another player.
She was also a teenager, and the pair "kind of just clicked," he tells the BBC.
He told her he liked her name, and she confessed that it was an alias. She was a runaway, she said - and was being held against her will, hundreds of miles from home, though she didn't know exactly where. The girl, 17, and had been missing for more than a year.
Stunned, Landon felt "helpless," he says - and, after learning more details over two weeks of chatting, he decided to tell his mother, Khristina on 31 October this year. The 41-year-old nurse and mother of five was putting Halloween makeup on her younger children for trick-or-treating when he briefed her.
That set the mother and son on a path to track down his friend, contact her mother, cooperate with the FBI - and ultimately witness the rescue of the teen - only 24 hours after Landon first alerted Khristina to her plight.
"She had one opportunity to reach out her hand and ask for help, and she chose me," Khristina says of the girl, who was 15 when she went missing.
A screenshot shows Khristina on a call with the girl as she showed her the knife her alleged captor kept under his pillow
The Tresps have shared with BBC screenshots of communication with the girl and a photo matching the criminal complaint to corroborate their story.
Landon first told his mother about "Jenny" - whose identity the BBC is protecting - in mid-October, a few weeks before the rescue.
"He had mentioned something about maybe a week or so into talking to her that he met a girl online, and she was really sweet," says Khristina - who cautioned him that "you don't always know who's on the other side of the screen".
"She's just having a really hard time and looking for a friend," he told her.
But Landon was becoming increasingly concerned as Jenny told him more about her situation.
They'd met playing Among Us, a game Landon describes as "kind of like online space Clue".
After telling Landon that she was a runaway, "Jenny" said an older man had taken her across state lines and wouldn't let her leave. She was the subject of a missing person investigation, and she sent Landon links to stories about her disappearance. But she believed police were no longer looking for her.
Jenny was scared and desperate, and that's why Landon went to his mother.
Her maternal instincts on high alert, Khristina contacted Jenny herself on Discord, the encrypted platform.
During the conversation, Khristina said she told the Colorado mother how she'd been through "years of abuse in her life and lots and lots of problems".
Within hours, Jenny started calling Khristina "mama".
Among Us supports cross platform play online with 4-15 players on various devices
The Colorado mother knew things were serious when she read the missing persons articles. Jenny knew she was in Oregon and gave the name of a city, but she didn't know where she was being held exactly. Khristina knew she needed more. She told Jenny to find a piece of mail or another document in the house that had a full name on it, which the girl did.
"That's when I went to work," Khristina says, delving into tax and property records.
Khristina narrowed down addresses, then searched them on a real estate site to find pictures. She showed the photos to Jenny, who confirmed that the second one was where she was being held.
The "next thing she asked me was to please not tell anyone until [her captor] was gone - that he did have weapons in the house and she was very scared," Khristina said.
Jenny promised Khristina she'd call her back through the game platform when he left the next morning, and in the meantime Khristina began looking for the law enforcement agency that had been assigned to the missing teen's case. She contacted Jenny's mother on social media, spoke briefly to her on the phone and then got a call from an FBI agent.
"Have you seen her alive?'" the agent asked Khristina.
"And I said: 'I have; I video chatted with her, I've seen her, and she goes 'Oh my God, I cannot believe any of this'," Khristina recalled.
When Jenny called Khristina back after her alleged captor left home, the FBI monitored their conversation. According to the criminal complaint's record of the conversation, Jenny explained how she'd met Adam Hunter Harmel on social media in May 2025.
He'd told her he was disabled and his hips were "messed up," offering Jenny money if she'd help get him to Oregon.
After he picked her up in Utah, however, Harmel threw her phone into a river, drove her to Oregon and kept her in the basement. He forced her to sleep against the wall in his bed, with a knife under his pillow, to prevent her from escaping. He gave Jenny a cell phone with no ability to make calls, but it could connect to wifi, which is how she played the online game.
The 39-year-old "would become violent and aggressive", the document says, which included hitting her and sexually assaulting her.
He also allegedly forced Jenny to remove her braces with pliers so she wouldn't be identifiable.
As Khristina and the FBI heard all of this, law enforcement were staging to bring Jenny to safety, after being alerted to her whereabouts.
While Harmel was out of the home, officers were sent to the street and the address, and Khristina was prepping Jenny for her run to freedom.
She'd unsuccessfully tried escaping before, she told Khristina.
Law enforcement was "phenomenal…giving me an update, you know, 'We're nine minutes out, we're seven minutes out,'" says Khristina, who was on the phone with Jenny the entire time, her son Landon watching at her side.
Khristina could hear other people in the home with Jenny, and she was afraid that someone would catch wind of what was happening and harm the girl.
But she kept any of those fears from Jenny.
"I want you to take three deep breaths with me," she told the teen. "When an officer tells me to go, and I relay that message to you, I want you to run up those stairs as fast as you can … Grab that basement door.
"I want you to keep going down that hallway and grab that front door… do not stop.'"
The mother and son watched breathlessly as Jenny ran into the arms of a state trooper.
Harmel is now in federal custody and has been charged in a criminal complaint with transportation with intent to engage in criminal sexual activity. Local Oregon media also reported he'd been accused of sexually abusing a six-year-old in the months before Jenny disappeared - and a sexual abuse protective order was granted against him in March 2025.
He remains behind bars awaiting trial.
A lawyer for the defendant did not respond to a BBC request for comment.
Jenny, meanwhile, remains in daily communication with Khristina and Landon - who still enjoys playing online games with her.
"Sometimes we just sit on video chat, just so she knows she has someone that cares," Khristina says. "She was on video last night when I cooked dinner …it's nice to know that when she has a bad day or a bad moment, she can call me right away or call Landon right away."
"She's doing great for what she's gone through."
They haven't met in person yet, but they're in the process of trying to make that happen.
"I hope I can put my arms around her soon," Khristina says.

script.intro: Guten Morgen und herzlich willkommen zu Ihren Sonntagsnachrichten! Wir starten direkt mit einem Blick auf die Wirtschaft und die großen Autobauer.

segments.headline: Japanische Autobauer standardisieren Teile zur Kostensenkung
segments.narration: In Japan schmieden die größten Autobauer, Toyota, Nissan und Honda, eine Allianz. Sie wollen ihre Teile standardisieren, um Kosten zu senken und so im globalen Wettbewerb, insbesondere gegen China, besser dazustehen. Zuerst geht es um Qualitätskriterien für Stahl, Plastik und Harze sowie um eine einheitliche Farbcodierung für Kabelbäume. Später sollen dann weitere Komponenten folgen, die man als Kunde aber meist gar nicht bemerkt. Dies wird nächstes Jahr anlaufen.
segments.summary_short: Toyota, Nissan und Honda standardisieren Teile, um Produktionskosten zu senken und ihre Wettbewerbsfähigkeit zu stärken.

segments.headline: IG Metall weitet Warnstreiks in Norddeutschland aus
segments.narration: Bleiben wir in der Wirtschaft, aber wechseln wir die Region. Die IG Metall Küste hat weitere 24-stündige Warnstreiks in der norddeutschen Metall- und Elektroindustrie angekündigt. Diese sollen teilweise schon am Sonntagabend beginnen. Betroffen sind unter anderem die Mercedes-Werke in Bremen und Hamburg, die Meyer Werft in Papenburg und Siemens Gamesa in Cuxhaven. Die Gewerkschaft fordert fünf Prozent mehr Gehalt bei einer Laufzeit von einem Jahr, während die Arbeitgeber eine deutlich geringere Erhöhung und eine längere Laufzeit vorschlagen.
segments.summary_short: Die IG Metall weitet Warnstreiks in Norddeutschland aus, um ihre Forderungen nach fünf Prozent mehr Lohn durchzusetzen.

segments.headline: Klimakonferenz COP31: Neuer Entwurf soll Durchbruch bringen
segments.narration: Von der Wirtschaft zum Klima: In Antalya ringen die fast 200 Staaten der COP31 weiterhin um eine Abschlusserklärung. Die Konferenz hätte eigentlich schon am Freitag enden sollen, aber der Streit um den Ausstieg aus fossilen Energien blockiert die Verhandlungen. Der türkische COP31-Präsident Murat Kurum hat nun einen neuen Textentwurf vorgelegt, von dem er hofft, dass alle Vertragsstaaten ihm zustimmen können. Es bleibt spannend, ob ein Kompromiss gefunden wird, der einen Rückschritt gegenüber früheren Klimabeschlüssen verhindert.
segments.summary_short: Die COP31 Klimakonferenz in Antalya verlängert sich, ein neuer Entwurf soll den Durchbruch im Streit um den Ausstieg aus fossilen Energien ermöglichen.

segments.headline: Mexikanischer Drogenbaron nach Schießerei festgenommen
segments.narration: Ein großer Erfolg im Kampf gegen die Kriminalität: Ein mexikanischer Drogenbaron, der auf der Liste der zehn meistgesuchten Verbrecher des FBI stand, wurde nach einer Schießerei mit mexikanischen Spezialkräften festgenommen. Fausto Isidro "Chapo Isidro" Meza Flores, Anführer der Meza Flores Organisation, und sieben weitere Personen wurden in Sinaloa gefasst. Bei der Operation kamen sieben Verdächtige und vier mexikanische Soldaten ums Leben. Die USA fordern seine Auslieferung, da er für die Überschwemmung der USA mit Fentanyl, Kokain und anderen Drogen verantwortlich gemacht wird.
segments.summary_short: Der auf der FBI-Liste der meistgesuchten Kriminellen stehende mexikanische Drogenbaron Fausto Isidro "Chapo Isidro" Meza Flores wurde nach einer Schießerei festgenommen.

segments.headline: FBI untersucht mutmaßlichen Hackerangriff auf Kriminalitätsdatenbank
segments.narration: Apropos FBI: Die US-Bundespolizei untersucht derzeit einen mutmaßlichen Hackerangriff auf ihre Kriminalitätsdatenbank, das National Crime Information Center (NCIC). Diese Datenbank wird von Bundes- und lokalen Strafverfolgungsbehörden genutzt, um Informationen über Haftbefehle und Hintergrundüberprüfungen auszutauschen. US-Präsident Donald Trump äußerte sich besorgt über den Vorfall, der nach einer Reihe von Technologieausfällen in der vergangenen Woche bekannt wurde. Experten betonen die Wichtigkeit des Schutzes dieser kritischen Informationen, auch wenn die Ursache der Ausfälle nicht in Cyberangriffen lag.
segments.summary_short: Das FBI untersucht einen mutmaßlichen Hackerangriff auf seine Kriminalitätsdatenbank, das National Crime Information Center (NCIC).

segments.headline: Sicherheitsvorfall bei Together AI: Prompt-Leakage bei KI-Anfragen
segments.narration: Ein weiterer Blick auf die digitale Sicherheit. Der KI-Dienstleister Together AI hat einen Sicherheitsvorfall gemeldet: Bei einem Teil der Prompts, die im Juni und Juli 2026 an den Serverless Inference Service gesendet wurden, kam es zu einem Datenleck. Ein unbefugter Dritter konnte gespeicherte Prompt-Samples herunterladen, nachdem Zugangsdaten für ein privates Repository in einem öffentlichen Code-Repository freigelegt worden waren. Das Unternehmen arbeitet eng mit externen Ermittlern und der Strafverfolgung zusammen und hat seine Sicherheitskontrollen verstärkt.
segments.summary_short: Together AI meldete einen Sicherheitsvorfall, bei dem Prompt-Samples aufgrund eines exponierten Zugangs in einem öffentlichen Repository kompromittiert wurden.

segments.headline: Nigerias Jugend: Warum sie die Wahl nicht prägt
segments.narration: Ein Blick nach Afrika, genauer gesagt nach Nigeria. Dort stellt sich die Frage, warum die junge Bevölkerung des Landes, die etwa 80 Prozent unter 40 Jahren ausmacht, die bevorstehenden Wahlen im Januar nicht stärker prägt. Trotz ihrer Fähigkeit zur Mobilisierung, wie bei den EndSars-Protesten 2020 und der 'Obedients'-Bewegung, ist die Wahlbeteiligung junger Menschen gesunken. Hohe Kosten für Wahlkampagnen und eine vorherrschende politische Kultur, die ältere Führungspersönlichkeiten bevorzugt, erschweren es jungen Kandidaten, sich durchzusetzen.
segments.summary_short: Trotz der Mehrheit der jungen Bevölkerung in Nigeria nehmen junge Menschen aufgrund finanzieller Hürden und traditioneller politischer Strukturen kaum Einfluss auf die bevorstehenden Wahlen.

segments.headline: Teenager rettet vermisstes Mädchen über Online-Spiel
segments.narration: Zum Schluss noch eine bewegende Geschichte aus den USA. Ein 16-jähriger Teenager aus Colorado hat zusammen mit seiner Mutter ein vermisstes 17-jähriges Mädchen gerettet. Die beiden lernten sich beim Online-Spiel 'Among Us' kennen. Das Mädchen war über ein Jahr lang vermisst und wurde gegen ihren Willen festgehalten. Nachdem Landon, der Teenager, seiner Mutter davon erzählte, konnten sie mit der Hilfe des FBI den Aufenthaltsort des Mädchens ermitteln und es befreien. Eine echte Heldentat, die zeigt, wie wichtig Aufmerksamkeit und Zivilcourage sind.
segments.summary_short: Ein 16-jähriger Gamer und seine Mutter halfen dem FBI, ein vermisstes Mädchen zu retten, das sie über ein Online-Spiel kennengelernt hatten.

script.full_text: Guten Morgen und herzlich willkommen zu Ihren Sonntagsnachrichten! Wir starten direkt mit einem Blick auf die Wirtschaft und die großen Autobauer. In Japan schmieden die größten Autobauer, Toyota, Nissan und Honda, eine Allianz. Sie wollen ihre Teile standardisieren, um Kosten zu senken und so im globalen Wettbewerb, insbesondere gegen China, besser dazustehen. Zuerst geht es um Qualitätskriterien für Stahl, Plastik und Harze sowie um eine einheitliche Farbcodierung für Kabelbäume. Später sollen dann weitere Komponenten folgen, die man als Kunde aber meist gar nicht bemerkt. Dies wird nächstes Jahr anlaufen. Bleiben wir in der Wirtschaft, aber wechseln wir die Region. Die IG Metall Küste hat weitere 24-stündige Warnstreiks in der norddeutschen Metall- und Elektroindustrie angekündigt. Diese sollen teilweise schon am Sonntagabend beginnen. Betroffen sind unter anderem die Mercedes-Werke in Bremen und Hamburg, die Meyer Werft in Papenburg und Siemens Gamesa in Cuxhaven. Die Gewerkschaft fordert fünf Prozent mehr Gehalt bei einer Laufzeit von einem Jahr, während die Arbeitgeber eine deutlich geringere Erhöhung und eine längere Laufzeit vorschlagen. Von der Wirtschaft zum Klima: In Antalya ringen die fast 200 Staaten der COP31 weiterhin um eine Abschlusserklärung. Die Konferenz hätte eigentlich schon am Freitag enden sollen, aber der Streit um den Ausstieg aus fossilen Energien blockiert die Verhandlungen. Der türkische COP31-Präsident Murat Kurum hat nun einen neuen Textentwurf vorgelegt, von dem er hofft, dass alle Vertragsstaaten ihm zustimmen können. Es bleibt spannend, ob ein Kompromiss gefunden wird, der einen Rückschritt gegenüber früheren Klimabeschlüssen verhindert. Ein großer Erfolg im Kampf gegen die Kriminalität: Ein mexikanischer Drogenbaron, der auf der Liste der zehn meistgesuchten Verbrecher des FBI stand, wurde nach einer Schießerei mit mexikanischen Spezialkräften festgenommen. Fausto Isidro "Chapo Isidro" Meza Flores, Anführer der Meza Flores Organisation, und sieben weitere Personen wurden in Sinaloa gefasst. Bei der Operation kamen sieben Verdächtige und vier mexikanische Soldaten ums Leben. Die USA fordern seine Auslieferung, da er für die Überschwemmung der USA mit Fentanyl, Kokain und anderen Drogen verantwortlich gemacht wird. Apropos FBI: Die US-Bundespolizei untersucht derzeit einen mutmaßlichen Hackerangriff auf ihre Kriminalitätsdatenbank, das National Crime Information Center (NCIC). Diese Datenbank wird von Bundes- und lokalen Strafverfolgungsbehörden genutzt, um Informationen über Haftbefehle und Hintergrundüberprüfungen auszutauschen. US-Präsident Donald Trump äußerte sich besorgt über den Vorfall, der nach einer Reihe von Technologieausfällen in der vergangenen Woche bekannt wurde. Experten betonen die Wichtigkeit des Schutzes dieser kritischen Informationen, auch wenn die Ursache der Ausfälle nicht in Cyberangriffen lag. Ein weiterer Blick auf die digitale Sicherheit. Der KI-Dienstleister Together AI hat einen Sicherheitsvorfall gemeldet: Bei einem Teil der Prompts, die im Juni und Juli 2026 an den Serverless Inference Service gesendet wurden, kam es zu einem Datenleck.
